the benzoquinone core is the key element for the activity and that a hydrophobic residue at position 5 and an aliphatic amino acid residue at position 3 seem to be optimal for prion replication inhibitory activities.
the benzoquinone core of 2,3-diaminobenzoquinone is the most promising scaffold for the development of new prion modulators.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quinacrine scaffold is the best one to target prions and that the amino acid moiety does not seem to be a critical factor in prion inhibition.
6a is a potent and selective inhibitor of prion replication in vitro, and that the quinone core and the L-amino acid methyl esters are the key elements for the activity of these compounds.
the benzoquinone moiety, when attached to a suitable scaffold, is a promising scaffold for the development of novel prion inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quinone core is the key element in the design of new quinone-based inhibitors.
the quinacrine core is a good scaffold to build new molecules for prion disease therapy.
the quinacrine scaffold can be modified in order to improve its prion inhibition potency and to reduce the risk of toxicity.
